related_questions.question: Is a COVID test tax deductible?
related_questions.snippet: According to the IRS, COVID-19 home testing kits are an eligible medical expense under the tax code. Personal protective equipment (PPE), such as masks, hand sanitizer and sanitizing wipes, are also eligible medical expenses if they're used primarily for preventing the spread of COVID-19.

related_questions.question: How long after exposure to COVID until you test positive?

text_blocks.snippet: Generally, it takes 3-5 days after exposure to COVID-19 for an individual to test positive, though this can vary based on the specific variant. The Omicron variant, for instance, has a shorter incubation period of around 3 days compared to 4-5 days for earlier strains. Testing too early after exposure, especially within the first 5 days, may result in a false negative.

list.title: General Timeline:
list.snippet: For most COVID-19 variants, it takes 3-5 days after exposure for the virus to replicate enough in the body to be detectable by a test.

list.title: Omicron Variant:
list.snippet: The Omicron variant tends to have a shorter incubation period, potentially leading to positive tests within 3 days of exposure.

list.title: Testing Too Early:
list.snippet: If you test too early, especially before the 5-day mark, your test may show a negative result even if you are infected. Medical sources say this is because there may not be enough virus in your system yet to be detected.

list.title: Testing After Exposure:
list.snippet: If you don't have symptoms but were exposed, wait 5 days before testing. If you test negative but want to be certain, take two more tests, 48 hours apart, health organizations recommend.

list.title: Positive Test Results:
list.snippet: If you test positive at any point, assume the result is accurate.
